answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to bonded collateral, so a coordinated equivocation event cannot be partitioned safely across aliases. If k identities sign conflicting state, correlated penalties scale as O(k^2), while detection applies an exponential capital-loss multiplier to the swarm’s aggregate escrow. A vine of aliases therefore offers no shelter: every thread of coordination raises exposure, and the tide of asymmetric depreciation can erase the operator’s remaining stake.
